issue.title: Neovim tabline crash on resize

repository.name: lightline.vim
repository.description: A light and configurable statusline/tabline plugin for Vim

issue.body:
## Env
  - Neovim: compiled from source to latest version (NVIM v0.5.0-593-g1ca67a73c)
  - OS: Debian testing up to date
  - lightline.vim: up to date

## How to Reproduce
  1. ```nvim -u vimrc -p vimrc vimrc```
  2. resize window
  3. neovim crashes with this error message: ```double free or corruption (!prev)```

where **vimrc** is: 
```vim
call plug#begin('~/.vim/plugins')
Plug 'itchyny/lightline.vim'
call plug#end()

let g:lightline = {
  \ 'tab' : {
  \   'active': [ 'mytabname' ],
  \   'inactive': [ 'mytabname' ]
  \ },
  \ 'tab_component_function' : {
  \   'mytabname': 'MyTabname'
  \ },
  \ 'separator': { 'left': '', 'right': '' },
  \ 'subseparator': { 'left': '', 'right': '' },
  \ }

function! MyTabname(n)
  return ""
endfunction
```

## Observations
  - this is a **neovim** bug, as **vim** works OK
  - this bug only happens when we have an **empty tab name** and **exotic seprators**

## Question
Do you know which section in **lightline.vim** code triggers this bug?
I tried to create a minimal testcase to open an issue in Neovim unsuccessfully.

Thanks in advance and thanks for the great plugin!
Antoine

body:
@antoinemadec Is it possible to use  ASAN enabled build or `valgrind` to get a little more information?

Related? #12500.

## Run
@erw7 , I ran valgrind like this:
```bash
valgrind -q                   \
  -q                          \
  --tool=memcheck             \
  --leak-check=yes            \
  --track-origins=yes         \
  --suppressions=.valgrind.supp \
  --log-file=valgrind-out.txt \
  --vgdb=yes                  \
  --vgdb-error=0              \
  --trace-children=yes        \
  ../build/bin/nvim -u vimrc vimrc
```

Then, ran **gdb**, open a tab in neovim with: ```:tabe vimrc``` and finally resized the window.
It crashed during resize.

## Logs
I kept on seeing messages like this one in **gdb** even before the crash:
```
Thread 1 received signal SIGTRAP, Trace/breakpoint trap.
0x00000000003bc638 in win_redr_custom (wp=0x0, draw_ruler=0)
    at ../src/nvim/screen.c:5395
5395	        tab_page_click_defs[col++] = cur_click_def;
```

**valgrind** also coroborate gdb's logs:
```
==79769== Invalid write of size 8
==79769==    at 0x3BC638: win_redr_custom (screen.c:5395)
```
and display the following message right after the last **continue**:
```
valgrind: m_mallocfree.c:303 (get_bszB_as_is): Assertion 'bszB_lo == bszB_hi' failed.
valgrind: Heap block lo/hi size mismatch: lo = 1344, hi = 0.
This is probably caused by your program erroneously writing past the
end of a heap block and corrupting heap metadata.  If you fix any
invalid writes reported by Memcheck, this assertion failure will
probably go away.  Please try that before reporting this as a bug.
```

Here are the full logs:
[gdb.log](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/files/4934590/gdb.log)
[valgrind-out.txt](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/files/4934591/valgrind-out.txt)

Please let me know if there is something else I can do to help.
@antoinemadec thanks. I don't know if it can be fixed, but I'll take a look.

When I revert 4ed654d9e8873a4ed3666396a215cfd6287b4ef7, it stopped happening. However, 4ed654d9e8873a4ed3666396a215cfd6287b4ef7 seems to be fine compared to the vim patch. So it is possible that the problem is with changes made prior to 4ed654d9e8873a4ed3666396a215cfd6287b4ef7.

@itchyny @erw7 , was the issue fixed by 4ed654d on Vim also present in Neovim?
If we remove 4ed654d, do we still see an issue with skipping empty statusline groups?

>  was the issue fixed by 4ed654d on Vim also present in Neovim?
If we remove 4ed654d, do we still see an issue with skipping empty statusline groups?

Perhaps neovim will have this problem too. Reverting 4ed654d will prevent it from passing the test, as shown below. Therefore, this change is necessary.

```
From test_statusline.vim:
Found errors in Test_statusline():
function RunTheTest[44]..Test_statusline line 265: Pattern '^{}\\s*$' does not match '{  }                                                                            '
```

I thought there was an unapplied vim patch, but it looks like all the vim changes to `build_stl_str_hl()` have been applied.

When I checked with `valgrind`, I found that the overflow was also occurring in `vim`, just without abnormal termination. I was able to fix it and created vim/vim#6505. I don't know how it will be fixed in vim, so if it is fixed in vim, I will port it.

@erw7 thats amazing. Thank you so much for debugging and fixing it!

Cheers!
